newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas slips early despite firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas slips early despite firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures slipped early Tuesday in moderate trade, following a soft close Monday and weakness on ACCESS, but some expected firmer cash and colder weather to limit the downside, sources said.
At 1205 EST, February slipped five cents to $2.565 per million British thermal units, while March was 4.7 cents lower at $2.26. Most others were down by one-half to 3.8 cents.

"We closed on a weak note yesterday, so it's a little continuation from that, but I like it here. Technically, we're holding above support and we could retrace back to the $2.93 area," said Cargill Investor Service's Thomas Blakeslee.
Technical traders saw March support along the trendline at $2.50 and then at the recent $2.46 low. Resistance was seen in the $2.70 area and then at $2.80.
Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report ranged from 120 to 152 bcf.
Temperatures in the Midwest are now expected to remain below-normal through the week. A cold front is also forecast for the Northeast by Thursday.
Most traders were surprised by the latest forecasts, which last week called for mostly above-normal weather for the eastern half of the nation into early February.
"The (revised) weather forecasts really caught us off guard. I wasn't expecting Houston to be in the 30s (F)," said one Houston-based trader.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed five to 10 cents early Tuesday to about the $3 level. Midcontinent pipes were up a similar amount to near $3 on colder weather in the region. New York city gate gas was quoted up to 20 cents higher at about $3.70.
NYMEX said 10,565 Hub contracts traded by 1135 EST. NYMEX Hub open interest on Jan 27 fell 3,774 contracts to 151,302.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1200 EST. February Alberta and Permian natgas expire Wednesday.

On the KCBT, February firmed 4.3 cents to $2.65, while March was one cent lower at $2.34. The March East/West spread narrowed by four cents to 22.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT open interest on Jan 27 rose 188 contracts to 2,576.
KCBT February natgas expires later today.
